title: NWEA College Explorer data visualization linking MAP Growth scores to higher-education benchmarks
description: The College Explorer is a data visualization from NWEA Research that, per the page, "links MAP® Growth™ scores with national benchmarks for colleges, universities, and even specific majors." It is designed to help students, parents, and teachers develop pathways to higher education, and is positioned as part of a broader planning process rather than a standalone report. The page categorizes it under innovations in reporting and assessment and college and career readiness for high school audiences.
requirements: Requires MAP Growth assessment scores as the input data linked to college and university benchmarks
constraints: The page frames it as one tool used "Together with goal setting and parent conferences," not as a sufficient standalone planner
target_learning_goals: Post-secondary planning and college and career readiness
examples: NWEA presents it on its Research site as a viewable interactive visualization under the topics Innovations in reporting & assessment, College & career readiness, and High school
key_sources: Kowalski, S. (2026). NWEA College Explorer. NWEA Research. https://www.nwea.org

article_title: A level playing field: College readiness standards
citation: Michael Dahlin and Beth Tarasawa. (2013). A Level Playing Field? How College Readiness Standards Change the Accountability Game. Northwest Evaluation Association. https://www.nwea.org
title: NWEA Growth Research Database and MAP computerized adaptive assessments
description: The Growth Research Database (GRD) is NWEA's longitudinal repository of Measures of Academic Progress (MAP) results; the full repository includes data from 4,800 school systems and approximately five million students. MAP tests are computerized adaptive assessments in mathematics, reading, language usage, and science for grades two through ten, scaled with a one-dimensional Rasch model on an equal-interval cross-grade scale. This study drew two intact cohorts of top-10% students, about 35,000 students across roughly 1,000 elementary and 400 middle schools in 31 states.
requirements: Students must have test information at all four test terms to be included in the cohorts
constraints: Only public schools were included, with about 5% of elementary and 6% of middle schools being charter or magnet schools; the report cannot claim the school sample represents the nation as a whole
target_learners: students in grades two through ten
target_learning_goals: measuring academic achievement and growth in mathematics and reading
examples: The elementary cohort comprised approximately 17,000 math and 19,000 reading high achievers tracked from third to fifth grade with four total measurements.
key_sources: Michael Dahlin and Beth Tarasawa. (2013). A Level Playing Field? How College Readiness Standards Change the Accountability Game. Northwest Evaluation Association. https://www.nwea.org/research/publication/a-level-playing-field-college-readiness-standards-whitepaper/
